DOCUMENT:
Budget Justification: Extended Opening Hours at Five Branch Libraries, 2027-28
Library Services, Westmoor Borough Council, September 2026

1. Request
Library Services requests a growth bid of £174,000 in the 2027-28 revenue budget to extend opening hours at five branch libraries (Ashgrove, Fenwick, Holt Lane, Kingsmead and Millbrook) by ten hours a week each, from 38 to 48 hours.

2. Rationale
The five branches currently close at 5 pm on weekdays and do not open on Sundays. Residents' surveys have repeatedly identified opening hours as the main barrier to library use among working-age adults: in the 2025 Residents' Survey, 44% of non-users aged 25-54 said the library "is never open when I can go". The Council Plan commits to increasing library use among working-age residents and to supporting adult learning and job-seeking.

Each branch would add late opening until 8 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays (six additional hours) and Sunday opening from 11 am to 3 pm (four additional hours).

3. Evidence from the Ashgrove pilot
From October 2025 to March 2026, Ashgrove trialled exactly this pattern, funded from one-off underspends.

Table 1. Ashgrove pilot: average visits per opening hour, October 2025 to March 2026
Time slot | Visits per hour
Weekday 9 am - 12 pm | 46
Weekday 12 pm - 5 pm | 58
Tuesday and Thursday 5 pm - 8 pm (new) | 21
Saturday 9 am - 1 pm | 64
Sunday 11 am - 3 pm (new) | 52

Over the pilot, Ashgrove recorded 1,140 new library memberships, compared with 690 in the same months a year earlier. Sunday sessions were particularly popular with families, and a weekly job club in the Thursday evening slot was fully booked from its third week.

Evening visits at Ashgrove averaged close to the weekday daytime level, which shows that there is strong latent demand for evening opening and that the new hours will be well used across all five branches.

4. Costs
Additional hours need two staff on duty at all times, in line with the Council's lone-working policy. Staffing is calculated on 50 weeks a year, allowing for bank holiday closures.

Table 2. Cost of extended hours, five branches
Item | Basis | Cost
Staffing | 10 hours x 2 staff x 50 weeks x 5 branches = 5,000 hours at £24.80 per hour (including on-costs) | £124,000
Utilities and caretaking | £6,500 per branch | £32,500
Self-service kiosk upgrades (maintenance contract) | 5 branches | £7,500
Total | | £174,000

The staffing rate is the mid-point of the Library Assistant grade plus 28% on-costs and an enhancement for Sunday working. Utilities and caretaking costs are based on the actual additional costs recorded at Ashgrove during the pilot, scaled to a full year.

5. Value for money
At current visit rates, the extra hours across the five branches would generate roughly 84,000 additional visits a year, at a cost of around £2 per visit. This compares favourably with the borough's average cost per library visit of £3.40.

6. Alternatives considered
We considered opening the branches with self-service access only in the extra hours, as some authorities have done. This would cut staffing costs by around two-thirds, but the Council's insurers have advised that unstaffed opening would require building alterations and CCTV at an estimated £60,000 per branch, and it would not support the job club and family activities that drove much of the pilot's success.

7. Risks
Recruitment. We expect to fill most additional hours from existing part-time staff who have asked for more hours, as happened during the pilot.
Demand at other branches. Ashgrove is our busiest branch, and demand at the other four may be lower. We will review usage after six months.

8. Conclusion
The twelve-month Ashgrove pilot has demonstrated strong demand for evening and Sunday opening, with new memberships up by two-thirds and evening use close to daytime levels. We ask Members to approve a growth bid of £174,000 to extend this successful model to all five branches from April 2027.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [arithmetic] at: "Total | | £174,000" -- The cost lines sum to £124,000 + £32,500 + £7,500 = £164,000, not £174,000. The growth bid is overstated by £10,000.
2. [inconsistency] at: "The twelve-month Ashgrove pilot has demonstrated strong demand" -- Section 3 states the Ashgrove pilot ran from October 2025 to March 2026, i.e. six months; the conclusion calls it a twelve-month pilot.
3. [misread_evidence] at: "Evening visits at Ashgrove averaged close to the weekday daytime level" -- Table 1 shows 21 visits per hour in the new weekday evening slot versus 46 and 58 in weekday daytime slots, i.e. less than half the daytime level. The text misstates the table, and the claim of strong evening demand rests on it.

REVIEW:
This is a bid for £174,000 a year to add Tuesday and Thursday evening opening and Sunday opening at five branch libraries. The case rests on a six-month pilot at Ashgrove, and the author's note stresses that both the demand evidence and the costing are firm.

Several things are good:
- **Real pilot data.** The bid uses measured visits from a pilot of the exact pattern being proposed, not projections.
- **Clear staffing calculation.** Hours × staff × weeks × branches is transparent and easy to check.
- **The lone-working requirement** is properly built into the staffing.
- **Honest risks.** The bid acknowledges that Ashgrove is the busiest branch.

But the table doesn't add up to the amount requested. The evening finding is the opposite of what the text says. And the value-for-money and self-service arguments don't hold on the bid's own numbers.

## 1. The costs sum to £164,000, not £174,000

£124,000 + £32,500 + £7,500 = **£164,000**. Either a £10,000 line is missing or the request is overstated. Whichever it is, the bid shouldn't go to Members with a total its own table doesn't support.

## 2. Evening demand is weak

Evening visits averaged **21 an hour**. Weekday daytime averaged about **54** (46 in the morning, 58 in the afternoon, weighted by hours). That puts evenings at under 40% of daytime use. The claim that evening visits were "close to the weekday daytime level" appears in the evidence section, the conclusion and the author's note, and the table contradicts it each time.

**Sunday is the strong result.** At 52 visits an hour it is close to weekday use. Splitting the costs by slot makes the contrast plain:

| Slot (per branch per week) | Staff-hours | Staffing cost | Visits (Ashgrove rates) | Staffing cost per visit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tue/Thu evenings (6 h) | 12 | ~£298 | 126 | **~£2.36** |
| Sunday (4 h) | 8 | ~£198 | 208 | **~£0.95** |

These are staffing costs only, at Ashgrove's rates. Evening opening costs about two and a half times as much per visit as Sunday opening, and it will cost more at quieter branches. The evidence supports Sunday opening clearly and evening opening weakly. That difference should be visible to Members.

## 3. The pilot ran for six months, not twelve

October 2025 to March 2026 is six months. The conclusion calls it a "twelve-month" pilot. A six-month winter pilot also leaves out summer, when Sunday and evening patterns may be different.

## 4. The visit projection uses the busiest branch for all five

The figure of 84,000 additional visits applies Ashgrove's rates to every branch: (6 × 21 + 4 × 52) × 50 weeks × 5 branches ≈ 83,500. But the risks section says Ashgrove "is our busiest branch" and the others may see less use. The projection should use each branch's own daytime usage as a scaling factor.

**Some of these visits may not be additional.** Existing users may simply shift their visit to an evening or Sunday. The pilot data could test this: did Ashgrove's *total* weekly visits rise compared with the year before, or only the visits during the new hours?

## 5. The value-for-money comparison doesn't compare like with like

The bid sets "about £2 per visit" against a borough average of £3.40. The £2 figure is a **marginal** cost: staffing and utilities for extra hours in buildings that already exist. The £3.40 average includes buildings, stock and management. Marginal cost will almost always look cheaper than average cost, so the comparison shows nothing. The fair comparison would be with the marginal cost of other ways to reach working-age non-users.

At the total actually costed, the figure is £164,000 / 84,000 = £1.95 per visit. That is still at Ashgrove's rates, so it is a best case.

## 6. The self-service comparison favours self-service after about four years

- **Self-service staffing saving:** about two-thirds of £124,000, or roughly **£83,000 a year**.
- **Building works:** £60,000 × 5 = **£300,000**, a one-off capital cost.
- **Payback:** about **3.6 years**.

So self-service is more expensive only in the first three or four years. Over any normal planning horizon it is cheaper. The comparison also sets a one-off capital cost against an annual revenue cost, and those come from different budgets.

The point that self-service can't host the job club or family sessions is fair. It argues for a **hybrid**, though, not for rejecting self-service entirely. For example: staffed Sundays and staffed job-club evenings, with self-service for the remaining evening hours. That option should be costed. The £60,000 figure is also an estimate attributed to the insurers. A quotation would make the comparison firmer.

## 7. Questions on the staffing and other costs

- **50 weeks.** Almost all bank holidays fall on Mondays or Fridays, so they rarely affect Tuesday, Thursday or Sunday hours. "Allowing for bank holiday closures" doesn't explain dropping two weeks. Christmas closures or leave might, so the basis should be stated.
- **Sunday enhancement.** The £24.80 rate includes a Sunday enhancement but appears to be applied to all 5,000 hours. If the enhancement is spread across evening hours too, show the rates for each slot.
- **Holiday cover.** Existing part-time staff taking on extra hours will accrue leave. It isn't clear whether cover for that leave is included in the 28% on-costs.
- **Utilities.** These are scaled up from a winter pilot, which probably overstates the annual figure. That makes this line genuinely conservative. Ashgrove's building may also not represent the other four.
- **Kiosk maintenance (£7,500).** It isn't clear why staffed opening needs this, or why it falls in this bid.

## 8. The membership increase isn't attributed to the new hours

Memberships rose from 690 to 1,140, which is +65%, so "about two-thirds" is accurate. But the bid has no comparison. Did memberships rise at other branches over the same months? Was there publicity or a joining drive linked to the pilot? Did a system change affect how memberships are counted? And how many of the new members joined during the new hours? The job club result ("fully booked from its third week") needs the number of places before it can carry much weight.

## 9. Risks

- **Recruitment.** Filling the hours from existing staff worked at one branch. Five branches need about 100 extra staff-hours a week, and the bid gives no evidence that there is that much demand among staff for extra hours.
- **The six-month review** has no decision rule. Set a threshold in advance, for example closing an evening slot at any branch that averages fewer than *n* visits an hour.

## On the author's description

| Claim in the note | What the document shows |
|---|---|
| "Evening visits running close to daytime levels" | 21 vs about 54 an hour, under 40% |
| Costs "sum to £174,000" | They sum to £164,000 |
| Self-service "would cost more once building works are included" | True only for about the first 3.6 years |
| Memberships "up by about two-thirds" | Accurate, but not attributed to the new hours |
| "Measured hour by hour" | The table gives averages by time slot |

## Suggested changes before this goes to Members

1. Correct the total, or add the missing £10,000 line.
2. Rewrite the evening claim to match Table 1, and present Sunday and evening opening as separate options with their own costs per visit.
3. Project visits for each branch, and test with the pilot's total-visit data whether visits are additional or shifted.
4. Replace the comparison with the £3.40 borough average with a marginal-cost comparison.
5. Cost a hybrid staffed and self-service option over at least five years.
6. Give the basis for the 50 weeks, and the hourly rate for each slot.
7. Add a membership comparison with other branches, and a decision rule for the six-month review.

A Sunday-first bid would be well supported by the evidence and cost less. Evening opening could follow as a smaller trial or a hybrid option.
